A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same visual-hierarchy learning method. All 24 pages of v2 and 22 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval experiments on HierOpenImages, LVIS and ten single-class datasets, plus cross-image sampling ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original HierOpenImages/LVIS experiments and ablations, and reports VOC/COCO results and new analyses of embedding distributions.

M1.justification: The within-image and cross-image entailment construction, shared encoder, hyperbolic projection and bidirectional contrastive angle loss remain unchanged. Equations (4)–(10) describe the same procedure; the new experiments do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: v2's ten single-class benchmarks—CIFAR-10/100, SUN397, Caltech-101, STL-10, Tiny-ImageNet, Food101, CUB, Pets and Flowers—are removed and replaced by VOC/COCO evaluation using ground-truth object boxes. v3 also adds blurred and extremely small crop scenarios. HierOpenImages and LVIS coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same CLIP, MoCo and HCL comparison configurations, including fine-tuned and Euclidean variants where previously evaluated. The replacement Table 4 still compares CLIP, CLIP-euc and CLIP-hyp; benchmark replacement does not change this comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 introduces ground-truth region proposals with top-5 voting for VOC/COCO. The new distribution analysis specifies Gaussian blur with sigma 5, 10 and 20, and samples of 100K full images and 100K bounding boxes. Core training budgets and retained tables' retrieval cutoffs are unchanged. Newly described noise filtering does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Figures 6 and 10 analyze how blur and extremely small sunglasses crops affect distance from the hyperbolic root, and compare full-image versus bounding-box distance distributions. These add sensitivity and representation analyses. The existing cross-image sampling ablation is retained, with v2 Tables 6–7 becoming v3 Tables 5–6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new embedding histograms describe sample distributions rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: The ten-dataset results in v2 Table 4 disappear. v3 Table 4 reports CLIP/CLIP-euc/CLIP-hyp scores of 87.3/92.2/93.9 on VOC and 63.6/66.5/71.8 on COCO; these are new-task results, not same-setting improvements. New plots report outward shifts for blurred/small crops and separation between full-image and part embeddings. Tables 1–3 and the matched appendix ablation tables retain identical values.

T1.justification: The Lorentz-space definitions, entailment relationships, angle formulas, losses and hierarchical retrieval metric in Equations (1)–(11) are unchanged. The appendix's Wasserstein expression is also retained. The new mechanism discussion adds no formal assumption, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: learning user-defined visual hierarchies without explicit hierarchical labels, enforcing pairwise entailment through contrastive angles, evaluating distribution alignment and generalizing beyond training hierarchies. The changed supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly interprets ambiguous, high-frequency crops' boundary placement as accommodating more angular entailment constraints and overlapping semantics through hyperbolic volume growth. v2 discusses hierarchical organization without this specific mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Appendices B.2–B.3 remove the explicit 5–30% evaluation area cutoffs and several candidate/class counts, including HierOpenImages' 59,691 full images and 330,063 boxes and LVIS's 14,716 images and 76,255 boxes. The removed single-class study's split and size documentation also disappears. v3 newly mentions excluding mislabeled or occluded samples, while optimizer, hardware and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: References associated with the removed single-class evaluations, including Food-101, SUN and Flowers, are dropped. The VOC/COCO protocol invokes Pal et al.'s already-cited compositional entailment work. Section 4 retains the same positioning relative to HCL and earlier hyperbolic entailment methods.

P1.justification: Author affiliations and footnotes change, several passages receive light wording edits, and Appendix B.3 is reorganized around LVIS and emergent structure. The abstract, principal section sequence and most explanatory prose remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively retypeset with different typography, headers, spacing and figure/table placement. The precision-recall and qualitative figures swap order, Table 4 is redesigned, and v2's dataset-size Table 5 is removed. The same new distribution panels appear in main Figure 6 and appendix Figure 10; existing appendix displays are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The VOC/COCO results and crop-sensitivity analysis add useful evidence. However, v3 removes exact filtering rules and candidate counts for retained HierOpenImages/LVIS results, and replaces the documented ten-dataset study with a briefly specified evaluation. The resulting loss of reproducibility and breadth of generalization evidence outweighs these limited additions, while the unchanged core method and results limit the overall decline.
